content: Epinephrine (aerosol) is a medication classified as an adrenergic, sympathomimetic, and bronchodilator agent. It is approved by the FDA for the temporary relief of symptoms such as shortness of breath, chest tightness, and wheezing caused by bronchial asthma. This medication works by relaxing the bronchial muscles, thereby improving airflow and alleviating asthma symptoms. Common side effects associated with its use include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, anxiety, sweating, and palpitations. Adult Indications and Dosage For adults, epinephrine (aerosol) is indicated for the temporary relief of asthma-related symptoms, including shortness of breath, chest tightness, and wheezing. It is used to control these symptoms by reducing bronchial muscle spasms. There is limited information available regarding off-label uses of this medication in adults. Pediatric Indications and Dosage There is insufficient information in the drug label regarding FDA-approved or off-label uses of epinephrine (aerosol) in pediatric patients. Contraindications The drug label does not provide detailed information on specific contraindications for epinephrine (aerosol). However, it is important to note that this medication should not be used without a confirmed diagnosis of asthma by a physician. Additionally, individuals who have been hospitalized for asthma or are currently taking prescription asthma medications should not use this product without medical supervision. Warnings This product contains substances such as dichlorodifluoromethane, dichlorotetrafluoroethane, and trichloromonofluoromethane, which are harmful to public health and the environment due to their ozone-depleting properties. Epinephrine (aerosol) is intended for oral inhalation only. Do not exceed the recommended dosage or frequency of use unless instructed by a physician, as excessive use may lead to nervousness, rapid heartbeat, or potential adverse cardiac effects. If symptoms persist or worsen within 20 minutes of use, discontinue the medication and seek immediate medical attention. Pregnant or nursing individuals should consult a healthcare professional before using this product. Keep this medication out of the reach of children. In the event of an accidental overdose, seek professional assistance or contact a poison control center immediately. Adverse Reactions Clinical trials have reported side effects such as nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, anxiety, sweating, and palpitations. There is limited information available regarding post-marketing adverse reactions. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy and Nursing Mothers: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of epinephrine (aerosol) during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Pediatric and Geriatric Use: There is no detailed FDA guidance on the use of this medication in pediatric or geriatric populations. Renal and Hepatic Impairment: No specific recommendations are provided for patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Immunocompromised Patients: There is no guidance on the use of this medication in immunocompromised individuals. Administration and Monitoring Epinephrine (aerosol) is administered via oral inhalation. The drug label does not provide detailed information on specific monitoring requirements during its use. Overdosage In cases of suspected overdose, contact the National Poison Help hotline (1-800-222-1222) immediately. Storage Do not puncture or incinerate the canister. Avoid storing the product near heat sources or exposing it to temperatures above 120°F, as this may cause the canister to burst. Store the medication at controlled room temperatures between 15°C and 30°C (59°F to 86°F). Patient Counseling Information Each inhalation delivers 0.16 milligrams of epinephrine at the mouthpiece. For adults and children aged 4 years and older, start with one inhalation and wait at least one minute. If symptoms persist, a second inhalation may be used. Do not use the medication again for at least three hours. Children under 4 years of age should only use this medication under the guidance of a physician. Before use, remove the dust cap, inspect the oral adapter for foreign objects, and shake the device well. To administer the medication, exhale fully, place the mouthpiece into the mouth, and press the canister down while inhaling deeply. Hold your breath as long as possible before exhaling slowly. Clean the plastic oral adapter daily by washing it with soap and hot water, rinsing thoroughly, and drying before reassembling the device. Alcohol Interaction The interaction between alcohol and epinephrine (aerosol) has not been established. Patients should consult their physician regarding the potential effects of alcohol consumption while using this medication.
